comparison: Perfect agreement on cell cycle profiling claims (C48, C49, C94, C95). Both evaluations support the quantitative measurements of cell cycle differences between NB4 and Kasumi-1 cell lines without concerns.
Perfect agreement on drug response claims (C50, C74-C76, C96-C97). Both evaluations support the G1 phase extension findings and the method's ability to detect drug effects on cell cycle progression.

Perfect agreement on G1/S transition discrimination claims (C77-C93). Peer reviewers identify this as 'the one potentially novel finding' and note detailed validation data. OpenEval also supports these claims but notes practical limitations for discriminating early vs. late S phase.
Strong agreement on machine learning pipeline claims (C44-C47, C99-C105, C107-C108). Both evaluations accept the automated analysis implementation and performance metrics without critique.
Agreement on RNA-seq validation claims (C52-C53). Both evaluations support the transcriptomic validation data demonstrating no perturbation from the imaging method.

Agreement on automation efficiency claims (C56-C62). Both evaluations accept the time savings and scalability improvements, though peer review focuses more on the automated nature while OpenEval details specific time comparisons.

Divergent evaluations on generalizability claims (C65-C67, C69-C71). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative without experimental validation. Peer reviewers support the broader applicability claims without challenge.

Partial overlap on core methodology claims. Both support the 72-hour imaging capability (C3, C25-C26, C31-C32, C63-C64), but peer review groups these with broader method validation claims (C4-C11, C68, C72-C73) that OpenEval evaluates separately.
Perfect agreement on adherent cell compatibility (C98). Both evaluations support the MDA-MB-231 data demonstrating applicability to adherent cells.

Partial overlap on image processing pipeline claims (C27-C29, C39-C43). OpenEval provides detailed technical evaluation, while peer review groups these with broader methodology validation without specific critique.

Overlap on summary capability claims (C4-C7, C11, C72). OpenEval notes these are summary statements supported by detailed results elsewhere. Peer review groups these with core methodology validation as part of overall method acceptance.

OpenEval evaluates background and context claims (C1-C2, C15-C23, C54) establishing limitations of traditional methods and FUCCI technology. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focus on novel findings rather than background.

OpenEval evaluates standard background claims about cancer biology and cell cycle regulation (C12-C14, C24). No corresponding peer review evaluation, as these represent established knowledge rather than novel contributions.

OpenEval evaluates technical challenge identification and preliminary validation (C30, C33-C35). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focus on final automated results rather than preliminary manual validation.

OpenEval evaluates technical challenge claims about alternating fluorescence (C36-C38). No corresponding peer review evaluation, though this challenge is implicitly acknowledged through acceptance of the image processing solution.
